materials.name: Optional: various ornaments - bells, fabrics, etc.

lessonSteps.text: take the clock clock and a single AA battry
open the battery case
insert the battery
close the lid
Make sure the clock is working and that the setting the alarm knob to the current hour triggers the alarm sound

In this stage we will be using a drill press and a 15mm drill bit for extracting the buzzer from the clock. if you do not have these however, its okay... the plastic cover protecting the buzzer is quite thin and can easily be discarded using a dremel tool, a hobby knife, heated x-acto knife, whatever works. follow through the instructions and modify to fit your tool of choice
make note of the buzzer location. usually it has a round hole just above it, for letting the sound out.
place the clock under the drill, right above the buzzer, and turn on the drill
slowly and gradually, lower the drill to uncover a round hole in the plastic right above the existing buzzer hole
the end result should look like this. gently reach for the buzzer and lift it, making sure not to pull the wires connected to it
make sure that the clock is still ticking after the minor surgery, including alarm
trim the wires attached to the buzzer, as close as possible to the buzzer itself
chop chop!
using a lighter, briefly heat the tip of each wire so that the plastic is melted away

before the wires are completely cold, with a slight finger pinch remove the melted plastic to expose the wires. easy on the pulling! these wires are pretty weak and will tear easily.  if need be, reheat before peeling
after cleaning, they should look like this
use an alligator clip to grab one of the wires. if the copper slips, fold the wire backwards onto the plastic isolation, and then grab both with the alligator
repeat with the second wire
cover any exposed wire by moving the alligator jacket to cover its teeth. then squeeze both alligators into the hole. from now on, try not to pull these wires
connect the other end of each alligator cable to a jumper wire, to allow incorporating the clock in the electronic circuit.
as so
take the usb cable and chop off its round end
expose approximately 2 centimeters of the black cable cover. press easy on the scissors' blade just enough to prevent the wire from slipping  while pulling the wire
expose about 1 centimeter of the black wire in the same manner.
after exposed, twist wire end with your index finger and thumb to bring copper threads together
repeat with the red wire. don't forget to twist (and shout)
you should end up with something like this
insert a jumper wire into the top-right hole on the breadboard, then take it out. repeat the process 3-5 times to loosen the breadboard springs before inserting the usb wires.

repeat the process one hole below.  
in the next slide you will be able to get a thorough explanation of what's a breadboard, how it's built, and how to use it

data.text: don't bend the metal part of the jumper wire as this might lead to breakage

lessonSteps.text: insert the red wire coming from the USB cable into the breadboard's top right row (R1).
repeat the process with the black wire, one row below
from now on we will use the schematic view of the circuit along with the photos
insert a red jumper wire into the same hole as the red usb wire. this will prevent it from slipping out of the hole
and a black jumper wire into the same hole as the black usb wire
locate the 555 chip. it is black and has 8 legs. notice the fact that the chip has a small circle embedded into one of its ends. this end will be our "north" from now on

data.text: what's 555? the 555 is a multi purpose swiss-knife of the electronics world, widely used in many maker projects, for example: motion detector, sound operated timer, audio amplifier, motor controller, timer switch, spot welder and many others

lessonSteps.text: insert the 555 chip into the center of the breadboard, rows  8-11, so that its north (dotted) end turns in the direction of the usb wires. be gentle when inserting, not to bend any of the legs
insert the TIP120 transistor to rows 15-17 on the right (R15-17), text facing the breadboard
Connect the red jumper wire to row R8 (8th row on the right)
Connect the black jumper wire to row L8 (8th row on the left)
locate the capacitor and spread its legs. notice which is the long leg and which is the short, as they reflect the capacitor's polarity
connect the capacitor between rows R2 (short leg) and R9 (long leg). be sure not to swap between the legs, as this will most surely cause the circuit to malfunction
locate the 100K resistor. it can easily be identified by its brown-black-yellow-gold color rings. see next slide to learn more about resistor color coding
bend resistors legs to nicely fit into the breadboard
connect the 100K resistor between rows R8 and R10. order of the legs does not matter as resistors aren't usually polarity-aware
connect another 100K resistor between rows R8 and L9
connect a jumper wire between rows R9 and R10

connect a jumper wire between rows L8 and R17, 
then another jumper wire between rows R1 and L11
locate the 2.2k resistor, color coded: red-red-red-gold
Connect the 2.2K resistor between rows L10 and R15
Connect wires coming from the alarm clock to rows L8 and L9. there is no good way to determine polarity, if the circuit does not trigger the toy, swap between these wires
temporarily remove the transistor to make room for the wires coming from the toy

connect wires coming from the toy to rows R16 and R17 and return the transistor to its original place, making sure to use the same holes as the wires. if upon inserting the transistor, toy starts working - swap between the wires
your circuit should now look like this
plug the usb cable into a power source
test! activating the alarm should trigger the toy. if not, try swapping between the wires coming from the clock, then double check the circuit
take the decorative plate and stick the wooden skewer into a 6mm hole in the center of the platform
attach the toy to the skewer using a zip tie
make sure to tie it well, not to allow the toy, once active, to climb off its prestigious pedestal
trim the zip tie
secure the breadboard to the plate using the sticker on its bottom
place near your bed until the dawn of a new day, new era!
